newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Thousands set off political activity in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Thousands set off political activity in Nigeria.

text.p: Thousands of people converged on a soccer stadium in eastern Nigeria on Thursday for a party convention that marks the resumption of political activity in Africa's most populous nation.
Politicians in gold-embroidered robes thronged the Owerri venue for the convention of the United Nigeria Congress Party (UNCP), largest of five political parties registered last month.
A band of traditional drummers entertained the 3,000-strong crowd. Hotels in the towns were full.
"We are the largest registered and Africa's number one party with close to 2.3 million members," Charles Obinna, local organising secretary of the United Nigeria Congress Party (UNCP) told Reuters.

Political activities were banned by military ruler General Sani Abacha who seized power in November 1993, in the aftermath of the chaos unleashed by the annulment of a presidential poll meant to have ended a decade of army rule and restored democracy.
Abacha has set a programme characterised by phased elections to hand over power to an elected president in October 1998.
But his critics say it is a ruse to perpetuate himself in power and point to the continued detention of many opposition figures including Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of the annulled vote.

In Lagos also, hundreds of delegates in flowing, colourful dress besieged a cricket pitch at the Tafawa Balewa Square for the first convention of the rival Congress for National Consensus (CNC) party.
Both have called the conventions to elect their leaders. For UNCP all three contestants for chairman are from the north, which suggests that its presidential candidate in 1998 could be a southerner.

Power-sharing has been at the root of Nigeria's political rivalry and under a draft constitution accepted by Abacha's government the vast African nation is split into six zones for the purpose of sharing important posts among the major groups.
"The post of chairman is zoned to the northwest, that is the reason why they are all from there," Obinna said. "This leadership election is all about democracy."
The party registration by the electoral commission sparked controversy when many groups that paraded the nation's best known politicians were not licenced.

Abacha's critics say the non-registration of parties with well-known politicians was a ploy to clear the way for him to run for the presidency, as has been the case with other military men in West Africa who have seized power and then won sham elections.
The infantry general has yet to respond to talk of him running for the presidency but some of his supporters insist he is as qualified as any other Nigerian if he wishes to contest.
"As far the UNCP is concerned, the possibility of the head of state standing is only a rumour," said Obinna.
"Our party is a welfare-oriented one. Its ideology is centrist, we take the best from the right, then the best from the left. Everybody who is a sound politician in this country is in UNCP."
